strategy.summary: Build NumPy at the buggy commit 874e163bbd6b and run the dtype string-parsing tests from the PR. On the buggy revision np.dtype('S') with size 2**61 is truncated through long-to-int and does not raise, so pytest.raises reports DID NOT RAISE (or the process crashes). On the fixed revision it raises TypeError or OverflowError and the tests pass. The expandtabs segfault is the user-facing symptom but the test diff exercises the dtype parser directly.

pip_packages: numpy build backend (meson-python, cython, spin as used by the numpy dev workflow)
system_packages: C/C++ compiler (gcc or clang) with a working Python dev header set
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/numpy/numpy && cd numpy && git checkout 874e163bbd6b && git submodule update --init
pinned_because: No numerically relevant pins: pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md Testing section with no constraint, era ceiling is null; latest versions compatible with the chosen Python are used, as an unbounded choice made by this plan.
Build backend requirements are taken from the repo requirements file at the buggy commit, not from the evidence context.

strategy.test_command: pytest numpy/_core/tests/test_dtype.py -k 'create_invalid_string_errors or invalid_types or leading_zero_parsing' -q
strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_dtype.py::test_create_invalid_string_errors (the new assertions: type(np.dtype('S'))(2**61) must raise TypeError or OverflowError; np.dtype('S1234hello') must raise TypeError), plus the S-1/U-1/V-1 assert_raises(TypeError) checks in test_invalid_types
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 874e163bbd6b the selected tests FAIL: type(np.dtype('S'))(2**61) does not raise (long-to-int truncation yields a small valid size), so pytest.raises reports DID NOT RAISE, or the interpreter segfaults, which also counts as failure. On the fixed revision the same selection PASSES: 2**61 raises TypeError or OverflowError, 'S1234hello' raises TypeError, and negative sizes raise TypeError.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.dtype('S') construction with size 2**61 via type(np.dtype('S'))(2**61), and np.strings.expandtabs(np.array('\t', dtype='S'), 2**61) as the original crash reproducer

input_output_examples.expected_output: an overflow error is raised instead of a segfault

risks: The test_strings.py diff adds the 2**61 call after a line that already raises OverflowError inside the same pytest.raises block, so the added call is unreachable and test_expandtabs_raises_overflow does not discriminate the bug; the transition must come from test_dtype.py.

The truncation-to-zero mechanism that makes 2**61 pass silently assumes LP64 (64-bit long, 32-bit int). On Windows (LLP64, 32-bit long) or 32-bit platforms the buggy path may already raise, so the transition may not occur there; the test's own comment says OverflowError on 32 bit.

Exact buggy behaviour (DID NOT RAISE versus segfault) is not stated in the evidence; the segfault is attributed to string_expandtabs_loop memset, which the dtype test may not reach, so a crash in the test process is possible and should be read as failure.
test_leading_zero_parsing (S010 == S10) is part of the same diff but is not established as failing on the buggy revision by the evidence; it may pass on both sides and does not carry the transition.
No explicit Python version is documented; python3.12 appears only in a traceback path, so python_version is left null and the chosen interpreter must be one NumPy at that commit supports.
Sanitisers or debug builds may change whether the memset path crashes; the plan uses a debug build for diagnosability, not because the evidence requires it.

Negative-size dtype behaviour (S-1) is implied by the test diff only; the context says the S-1 failure was seen with a fix in PR discussion, so the S-1 asserts may be the least certain part of the transition.

oracle.reference_source: Exception type asserted by pytest.raises in numpy/_core/tests/test_dtype.py (TypeError or OverflowError)
oracle.why: The transition is decided by whether an exception of the stated type is raised, not by a numerical value.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: pytest.raises(TypeError, OverflowError) receives no exception from type(np.dtype('S'))(2**61) because the long value is cast to int and wraps to a small size, so the block completes and pytest reports DID NOT RAISE; a segfault during the call would also abort the test as a failure.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed revision detects the overflow when parsing the size and raises OverflowError or TypeError, satisfying pytest.raises, and raises TypeError for 'S1234hello' and negative sizes, so the selected test passes.
